extracted.intended_audience: authors of the manuscript, peer reviewers, editors, and readers interested in best practices for research software registries and repositories
extracted.subtask_description: Peer review history for a submitted manuscript proposing nine best practices for research software registries and repositories; includes reviewer evaluations focused on reporting, experimental design, validity, and actionable suggestions to improve clarity, evidence, and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of writing clarity, completeness of literature references, consistency of author list and terminology, and the presentation of best practices and examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the paper is generally well-written and easy to follow; include proper literature citations for named archives (e.g., swMATH, Software Heritage, FigShare) rather than URLs only; anticipate and introduce key terminology (e.g., 'resources and collections') early and be consistent; ensure author list in manuscript matches submission system and relegate non-authors to acknowledgements; fix typographical issues such as incorrect quotation marks. Make the main text self-contained by including 1–2 concrete examples inline after each best practice and cross-reference the appendix for additional examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design / Methodology reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation and presentation of the survey or empirical methods used to derive the best practices, including all questions asked and the responses obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document all survey questions (not just a subset), provide descriptive statistics (raw counts and percentages) and/or visualizations to substantiate empirical grounds, and present an overview (e.g., Table/Figure 1) of responses such as repository name, starting year, number of records, target audience, and services provided. Consider using a table rather than a figure to save space; if using figures, try stacked bar or divergent stacked bar charts given three-response options (Yes/No/Other). Integrate Appendix C into the Methodology if it contains needed survey detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of the findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviewer concerns about interpretation, wording, and completeness of best practice statements have been addressed and whether the findings are supported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to and incorporate reviewer points in the manuscript (not only in the rebuttal). Clarify awkward or redundant wording (e.g., best practice 4.1's 'what is accepted' vs 'what is not accepted' and 'notable exceptions'); ensure recommendations are actionable and justified by the presented evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include inline examples for best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation practice recommending at least 1–2 concrete examples inline in the main paper text immediately after each best practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the main text self-contained and more engaging by placing examples inline with the best practice; reserve the appendix for additional examples. This applies to all best practices because they all have examples in Appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full survey/question instrumentation and summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Make available the full list of questions asked and summarize responses so readers can assess the empirical basis for the guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the complete questionnaire and summary statistics (counts/percentages) for each question, and direct readers to the appendix for full detail if needed. This supports transparency and allows readers to judge the relevance of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present descriptive statistics / visualizations of survey results
rubrics_metrics.description: Use descriptive statistics and visual aids to substantiate empirical claims about adoption rates and characteristics of surveyed registries/repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a table or figure summarizing responses (e.g., counts and percentages for Yes/No/Other). Suggested visualization types: stacked bar chart or divergent stacked bar chart. Use a table if space is a concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate Appendix C into Methodology when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Move methodological details or summary results from appendices into the main Methodology section to strengthen the empirical basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Appendix C contains survey details that support the development of best practices, include key elements or summaries in Methodology and keep the appendix for full data or extended material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensively cite relevant archives and literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that important repository/registry projects and related literature are cited formally, not just by URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add literature references for services such as swMATH, Software Heritage, and FigShare (examples provided), and include references for organizations/initiatives mentioned (e.g., RDA, FORCE11) so unfamiliar readers can follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt and use a single, clear term for the objects of the guidelines (e.g., 'resources' vs 'collections' vs 'registries and repositories').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and introduce the chosen term early in the introduction and use it consistently through the paper to reduce reader fatigue and ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overclaimed scope statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone down statements that assert the guidelines 'address the needs' of domain software registries and repositories if the paper only provides guidelines rather than fulfilling those needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rephrase claims to reflect the paper's actual contribution (guidelines/recommendations) rather than implying comprehensive coverage or solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify wording of specific best practices (4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the language of individual best practices precise and unambiguous, especially regarding what is required versus optional and the intended scope (metadata vs data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from reviewers: reword 4.1 to focus on criteria/properties of acceptable artifacts rather than restating complements; change 'share your metadata schema' to 'publish' or 'document' to emphasize public availability; reframe 4.3 as 'required and optional metadata expected for deposited software' rather than centering on who provides metadata; clarify 4.4's relation to citation policies; generalize 4.6 to address both metadata and actual software (use '(meta)data').

rubrics_metrics.name: Be decisive about recommended actions (avoid ambiguous modal verbs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid weak or ambiguous recommendations phrased with 'can', 'may', or similar modal verbs; prefer clear prescriptions or explain the modal semantics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either take a stance (make requirements/recommendations explicit) or define the exact meaning of modal verbs used (e.g., adopt RFC 2119-style language) so resource operators know whether to implement an item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document retention/backup and takedown handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When recommending policies for taking data offline and archiving, include requirements to document backup/retention strategies and procedures for legal takedown notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify retention policies (backup strategy), and describe how archives respond to legal takedown requests (e.g., DMCA, GDPR) so operators and users know archive behavior in legal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify migration targets when mentioning migrations (e.g., Zenodo example)
rubrics_metrics.description: When stating that data will be migrated, indicate the destination archive to which data will be moved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the migration target makes migration commitments actionable and informative for users and depositors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure rebuttal actions are reflected in manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not address reviewer concerns only in the rebuttal letter; insert corresponding edits into the revised manuscript so readers see the changes without the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PeerJ Staff guidance on preparing rebuttal letters and ensure manuscript text is updated where appropriate; readers should not need to consult the rebuttal to understand the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clarity / correct errors in the paper metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct inconsistencies or factual errors in figures/tables/captions and dates (e.g., Task Force meeting date vs Table 1 caption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify dates and labels for internal consistency; fix any random mistakes that could confuse readers about the timing or provenance of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation choices: prefer tables for certain survey summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider using a table instead of a figure to present survey result summaries to save space and present counts/percentages more compactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the survey responses are three-option categorical data summing to a known total (e.g., 30), a table presenting raw counts (%) may be more appropriate than separate bar charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor editorial corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix small issues such as incorrect quotation marks or LaTeX rendering problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address typographical/formatting problems as part of revision to improve readability and professional presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide follow-up impact tracking and comparison to related guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest future work to track adoption/impact of the proposed best practices and to compare similarities/differences with guidelines developed for data repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a plan or suggestions for impact assessment and explicitly discuss how these best practices align or diverge from existing data repository guidelines.
